document_check.note: The document is Hamilton CA, Schumacher J, Matthews F, Taylor JP, et al. 'Slowing on quantitative EEG is associated with transition to dementia in mild cognitive impairment', International Psychogeriatrics (2021) 33:12, 1321-1325. The 92 MCI participants with qEEG (36 MCI-AD, 17 possible MCI-LB, 39 probable MCI-LB) were analysed with a multistate competing-risk model (msm), which matches the cited description.

cited_result: The context cites the cohort (92 MCI patients) and the analysis (multistate model). The principal result of that analysis is appraised: baseline qEEG theta/alpha ratio and transition from MCI to dementia, HR 1.84 (95% CI 1.01 to 3.35) per 1 SD increase, p = .046. The model is a multistate competing-risk model with death as a competing state, adjusted for age, ACE-R and aetiology, with 14 incident dementias and 5 deaths.
tool_reason: The result is the association of a single prognostic factor (baseline qEEG slowing) with a later outcome (incident dementia), adjusted for covariates, not the development of a prediction model, so QUIPS applies.

domains.rationale: The source population, inclusion and exclusion criteria, and baseline characteristics are described. Eligibility required possible DLB features in the records, so the sample is enriched and not a general MCI population. The recruitment method (consecutive or not) and participation rate are not reported. Eleven of 103 MCI participants lacked qEEG, with no reasons or comparison given.

signalling.question: Adequate description of source population and recruitment
signalling.quote: "These were recruited from older persons healthcare and memory services in North East England. All were aged ≥60 years, had a health service diagnosis of MCI, and were considered for eligibility if their medical records reported the possible presence of any core clinical features of DLB"

signalling.question: Adequate participation (recruitment method, participation rate)
signalling.quote: Searched for consecutive or random sampling, number approached, number declining; none reported. Only: "One-hundred and three participants with MCI were included in a longitudinal study"

signalling.question: Inclusion and exclusion criteria adequately described
signalling.quote: "absence of objective cognitive impairment, presence of parkinsonism for longer than 12 months prior to the onset of cognitive symptoms, or presence of possible frontotemporal or vascular etiologies"

signalling.question: Baseline study sample adequately described
signalling.quote: "Table 1. Baseline characteristics of cohort with qEEG available"; "AD (N = 36) POSSIBLE LB (N = 17) PROBABLE LB (N = 39)"

signalling.question: Sample with prognostic-factor data representative of those enrolled
signalling.quote: "data were not available for 3 comparators and 11 MCI." (no reasons or comparison with those analysed)

domains.rationale: Deaths are handled as a competing state. The number of participants lost or with no follow-up visit, the reasons, and how they compare with those followed are not reported, although follow-up ranges start at 0 years in every MCI group and visits were rescheduled during COVID-19.

signalling.question: Proportion of sample with follow-up data adequate and loss described
signalling.quote: "Follow-up years 1.09 [0.12, 2.32] 1.00 [0, 3.61] 1.03 [0, 3.63] 1.99 [0, 3.67]" (no count of participants without follow-up or lost)

signalling.question: Reasons for loss to follow-up provided
signalling.quote: Searched for dropouts, withdrawals or loss to follow-up; only "After diagnosis of dementia, participants were withdrawn from further follow-up." and "adaptive scheduling necessitated by COVID-19 from 2020"

signalling.question: Competing events handled
signalling.quote: "This model accounted for death as a competing outcome"

signalling.question: Participants lost to follow-up similar to completers
signalling.quote: Searched for any comparison of participants lost versus followed; none reported.

domains.rationale: Theta/alpha ratio is clearly defined and measured at baseline with one standard 128-electrode protocol for all participants, before any outcome occurred. It was analysed as a continuous z-score. Data were available for 89% of enrolled MCI participants.

signalling.question: Clear definition of the prognostic factor
signalling.quote: "Mean band power within the theta (4–5.5 Hz) and alpha (8–13 Hz) frequency bands was calculated as described previously (Schumacher et al., 2020), and the average theta/alpha ratio across all electrodes was computed."

signalling.question: Method of measurement valid, reliable and the same for all participants
signalling.quote: "all included participants were offered EEG recording at baseline. Resting state eyes-closed EEG was recorded from 128 electrodes using Waveguard caps (ANT Neuro)."; "visual inspection and exclusion of noisy channels and epochs"

signalling.question: Continuous variable handled appropriately
signalling.quote: "Theta/alpha ratios and ACE-R scores were standardized into Z-scores from the healthy group data"

signalling.question: Adequate proportion with complete prognostic-factor data
signalling.quote: "data were not available for 3 comparators and 11 MCI." (92 of 103 MCI analysed)

domains.rationale: Dementia has a clear clinical definition and is judged by an independent three-psychiatrist panel. The document does not say the panel was blinded to qEEG (blinding is stated only for the imaging raters). Assessment timing varied because of COVID-19 rescheduling.

signalling.question: Clear definition of the outcome
signalling.quote: "A diagnosis of dementia was made when the participant was judged by the panel to no longer function independently, thus not meeting the criteria for MCI."

signalling.question: Valid and reliable method of outcome measurement
signalling.quote: "At baseline and after each follow-up, a three-person panel of experienced old age psychiatrists independently reviewed research notes from the clinical interview"

signalling.question: Outcome assessed blind to the prognostic factor
signalling.quote: Searched for blinding of the diagnostic panel to EEG results; blinding is reported only for imaging: "images were visually rated as normal or abnormal by a panel of trained image analysts, blind to diagnostic information"

signalling.question: Same method and setting of outcome measurement for all participants
signalling.quote: "longitudinal follow-up (initially at 12-month intervals, but with adaptive scheduling necessitated by COVID-19 from 2020)"

domains.rationale: The primary model adjusts for age, baseline ACE-R and aetiology. Sex and education were left out because they were non-significant in another cohort. Cholinesterase-inhibitor use, which is unevenly distributed (46.2% in probable MCI-LB versus 19.4% in MCI-AD) and plausibly affects EEG, enters only a sensitivity analysis.

signalling.question: Important potential confounders measured
signalling.quote: "Receiving cholinesterase Inhibitors 0 (0%) 7 (19.4%) 3 (17.6%) 18 (46.2%)"

signalling.question: Important confounders accounted for in the primary analysis
signalling.quote: "controlled for additional hazards with a theorized association with a faster decline to dementia including chronological age (centered at 74 years) and baseline global cognitive performance (Addenbrooke’s Cognitive Examination – Revised [ACE-R] Total Score)"; "with etiology included as a covariate"

signalling.question: Covariate selection appropriate
signalling.quote: "Gender and education, which were not found to significantly predict dementia transitions in a larger cohort (Hamilton et al., 2021), were not included as covariates."

signalling.question: Confounding by medication addressed
signalling.quote: "In a further analysis instead controlling for use of cholinesterase inhibitors in MCI, again this effect was no longer evident (HR = 1.80, 95%CI: 0.97–3.32)."

domains.rationale: Only 14 dementia events support a model with the factor plus age, ACE-R and a three-level aetiology covariate, which gives very few events per parameter and a risk of sparse-data bias. Transition times are treated as exactly observed, although dementia was established by panel review after scheduled visits. Model assumptions are not reported as checked, and there is no protocol. Sensitivity analyses are reported openly.

signalling.question: Sufficient presentation of data to assess adequacy of analysis
signalling.quote: "hazard ratio (HR) = 1.84, 95% CI: 1.01–3.35 per 1 SD increase in theta/alpha ratio, Z = 1.99, p = .046"

signalling.question: Strategy for model building appropriate (events relative to parameters)
signalling.quote: "Fourteen cases of dementia were observed following baseline diagnosis of MCI (mean = 1.5 years after baseline, SD = 0.5)"; "the absolute number of dementia cases was low."

signalling.question: Selected statistical model adequate for the design
signalling.quote: "This model accounted for death as a competing outcome, with exactly observed transition times" [p3]; "For MCI patients, follow-up assessments took place approximately 12, 24, and 42 months from baseline." [p2]

signalling.question: No selective reporting of results
signalling.quote: "In a sensitivity analysis controlling for the presence of complex visual hallucinations and cognitive fluctuations ... this effect was no longer evident (HR = 1.17, 95% CI: 0.66–2.07)."

applicability.rationale: Eligibility required possible DLB features in the medical records, so 56 of 92 analysed participants are possible or probable MCI-LB. The estimate applies to an LB-enriched MCI sample, not to unselected memory-clinic MCI.

overall_rationale: Statistical analysis is at high risk: 14 events against several covariates, and exact transition times assumed for visit-based diagnoses. Participation, attrition, outcome measurement and confounding each carry moderate concerns. By the QUIPS rule (any high, or three or more moderate) the overall rating is high, consistent with the authors' own description of 'early, marginal evidence'.
